summary: Firelookout.ca lists a Lanark Fire Tower at 45.1175, -76.37417 under a Tweed address; no height, build year or status is recorded.

evidence.supports: Entry is named Lanark Fire Tower
Entry address is given as Tweed, ON
Entry says the tower appears on Pembroke topographic map 31F of 1996 but not on the Tower Detection System Map
evidence.quote: Appears on Pembroke topographic map 31F, 4th, ed., 1996. Does not appear on Tower Detection System Map.

evidence.supports: Design idea: tall structure on a peak, a person living in it, reporting fires to crews
evidence.quote: The idea was simple: Build a tall structure on a hill or mountain peak, hire someone to live in it, and have them report fires to teams on the ground.

evidence.supports: At their peak Ontario had 325 lookouts
evidence.quote: At their peak, the towers sprawled throughout North America, with 325 lookouts across Ontario alone.

evidence.supports: Towers in forested terrain were built of wood and later steel, with a small platform for the lookout
evidence.quote: In more forested terrain, wood, and later steel, was used to build a tower with a small platform for the lookout to live.

evidence.supports: As of 2013, the Ontario ministry had decided to remove many still standing towers
evidence.quote: The Ontario MNR has decided, as of 2013, to remove many of these still standing towers.

sources.title: The History of the Fire Tower: From World War II to Jack Kerouac to Temagami

notes_for_editor: Thin record. Firelookout.ca is the only source for this tower; it is not in the Ontario tower layer, and no other page was found after one search. The address reads Tweed, ON, but the coordinates 45.1175, -76.37417 are roughly 100 km from Tweed by my own rough reckoning, which suggests the Lanark area instead. The story keeps the directory's address as printed and names no county. Please confirm the location (and whether the Tweed address is a placeholder) before publishing. Nothing is known about the site today.
